prompt: In an underwater laboratory, a small yellow submarine is docked next to a large, glass-domed research station. A giant octopus is wrapping one of its tentacles around the submarine. The smooth, metallic hull of the submarine contrasts with the soft, organic skin of the octopus. The submarine has a propeller on its back. A long robotic arm, which is a component of the research station, is extending towards the octopus, holding a glowing sample container. The octopus has two tentacles touching the station's dome. A group of fish is swimming between the octopus and the submarine, and their number is three times the number of tentacles touching the dome. The research station is built on top of a massive piece of glowing coral. The octopus is facing the research station. The submarine's front viewport is facing away from the station. The robotic arm is pushing some loose rocks away; the number of rocks is one more than the number of tentacles touching the dome. The glowing coral is the brightest light source. A diver in a wetsuit is swimming under the robotic arm, holding a camera and pointing it at the octopus. The diver's modern wetsuit appears newer than the slightly scratched viewport of the submarine. The robotic arm has a claw at its end. The submarine is connected to the station with a flexible tube.
